issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or shifts hard
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, the engine revving between gears, slipping, or loss of a gear (often 3rd and 4th, or reverse).
issues.why: Every Envoy uses GM's 4L60-E automatic. Heat and wear break down its clutch packs, seals and valve body parts, especially in a heavy SUV or one that tows.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't engage a gear, have it diagnosed before driving far; continued driving usually turns a repair into a full rebuild.

issues.t: Central 'spider' fuel injector misfires or floods a cylinder
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, a check engine light, hard starting, or a fuel smell. A leaking nozzle can flood a cylinder after the engine sits.
issues.why: The 4.3L V6 in the original Envoy uses one central injector that feeds each cylinder through thin lines and small poppet nozzles. With age the nozzles stick or clog and the lines can leak.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed. Replacing the whole spider assembly is the normal fix and is often done along with the intake gaskets.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, coolant crust around the intake, or milky oil if coolant gets inside the engine.
issues.why: The intake manifold gaskets on this Vortec V6 break down over time and let coolant seep out or into the oil.
issues.next: Don't let it run low on coolant or overheat. Replace the gaskets soon; if coolant has reached the oil, change the oil right away to protect the bearings.

issues.t: Center console lid can pop open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the console lid may feel like it releases easily.
issues.why: The console lid latch could let go with less force than federal rules allow, so the lid or what's inside could hit someone in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the latch free.

issues.t: Daytime running lights drown out the turn signals (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers may have trouble seeing your turn signals because the daytime running lights stay on bright next to them.
issues.why: The daytime running lights were too bright and too close to the turn signals and did not shut off when they flashed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs and programs a new body control module free.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads empty when the tank is full, sticks, or swings back and forth; the low fuel light may come on at the wrong time.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor inside the tank wears or its contacts get fouled, so it sends a bad reading.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. The sender is part of the in-tank fuel pump module, so it's often replaced with the pump.

issues.t: Cooling fan roars all the time or engine runs hot
issues.sym: A loud roaring fan whenever the engine runs, or the opposite: the temperature climbs in traffic or with the A/C on.
issues.why: These SUVs use an electronically controlled fan clutch. When it fails it can lock up and run nonstop, or slip so the fan doesn't pull enough air.
issues.next: Have the fan clutch and its wiring checked. If the engine is running hot, don't keep driving it; overheating can damage the engine.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel or temperature gauges stick, read wrong or drop to zero.
issues.why: Small stepper motors that drive the gauge needles wear out inside the cluster.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. A cluster repair shop can replace the stepper motors for less than a new cluster.

issues.t: Cracked fuel filler neck leaks gas
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell, fuel dripping near the rear wheel on the fill side, or a check engine light for an EVAP leak.
issues.why: The filler neck between the gas cap and the tank rusts or cracks, so fuel can leak when the tank is filled.
issues.next: A fuel leak is a fire risk. Don't top off the tank and get the filler neck replaced right away.

issues.t: Rear air suspension sags from a failed compressor
issues.sym: The rear of the SUV sits low, rides rough, or the compressor runs a long time or not at all.
issues.why: On models with the optional rear air suspension, the air compressor wears out, and leaking air springs make it work harder.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before replacing the compressor. Many owners switch to conventional coil springs instead.

issues.t: Blower runs on one speed, quits, or stays on
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan won't run, works on only one speed, or keeps running with the key off.
issues.why: The blower motor control module fails.
issues.next: Replace the blower control module. If the fan keeps running with the key off, it can drain the battery, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Power window popping, slow or falling down
issues.sym: A pop when raising the window, a slow window, or glass that drops into the door.
issues.why: The plastic guides and cable in the window regulator wear or break.
issues.next: Replace the window regulator. If the glass has dropped, tape it up or keep it closed until it's fixed.

issues.t: Groan or shudder when turning at low speed
issues.sym: Groaning and shudder from the steering mostly when parking or turning slowly.
issues.why: GM traced it to the steering gear on these SUVs and released a redesigned gear.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level first. If it's full, a shop can confirm the steering gear and replace it.

issues.t: Liftgate glass is hard to close
issues.sym: The flip-up rear window needs a hard slam or won't latch.
issues.why: The weather strip around the rear glass gets stiff with age.
issues.next: A softer replacement weather strip and a small shim usually fix it.

issues.t: Engine burns too much oil
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, and a low oil warning may come on. Owners report it around 70,000 miles.
issues.why: Oil consumption is the top engine complaint for the 2006 Envoy; the source of the leak or burning varies from truck to truck.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it full. Have a shop look for leaks and run an oil consumption test before deciding on bigger repairs.

issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, sometimes restarting after a moment.
issues.why: Stalling is one of the most-reported 2003 Envoy problems. Causes vary, so it needs proper diagnosis.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Stalling is dangerous in traffic. Have the codes read and the fuel and ignition systems checked soon.

issues.t: Air suspension can make the engine stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls and may not restart.
issues.why: Electrical spikes from the electronic air suspension could upset the engine computer.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs a wiring harness free.

issues.t: Transfer case may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV may roll even with the shifter in Park, or the transfer case loses gears.
issues.why: A transfer case control calibration could keep it from fully engaging, and a range shift collar could crack.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN; a dealer updates the module or replaces the transfer case free.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bracket can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, wandering steering, or in the worst case the wheel moving out of place.
issues.why: The frame brackets that hold the front lower control arms could fracture.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces both brackets free.

issues.t: Fuel filter line can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, a no-start, stalling, or sudden heavy steering after a stall.
issues.why: A fuel line connection at the fuel filter could disconnect.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving. Check your VIN; a dealer replaces the retainers free.

issues.t: Rear floor may be missing welds (recall)
issues.sym: No visible sign.
issues.why: Some early trucks were built without rear floor welds, which can weaken third-row seat and seat belt anchors in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. GM inspected these trucks and bought back or replaced those missing welds.

issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The driver air bag inflator could crack at a weld when it fires, sending fragments toward occupants and leaving the bag underinflated.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects and replaces the air bag free.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may not power up (recall)
issues.sym: The gauges and warning lights stay dark when you start the engine.
issues.why: A software problem could keep the instrument cluster from turning on at start-up.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer reprograms the cluster free.

issues.t: Left front brake line can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A longer pedal travel and weaker braking, or brake fluid near the left front wheel.
issues.why: A scratch made during manufacturing could make the left front brake pipe fracture.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the brake pipe free.

issues.t: Wipers stop or washer pump keeps running (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers quit, run on their own, or the washer pump keeps squirting.
issues.why: Water can get into the wiper control module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer seals the module and replaces wiper parts as needed, free.

issues.t: Key and shifter can move out of Park with the engine off (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key with the shifter out of Park, or move the shifter out of Park with the ignition off.
issues.why: Mechanical overrides on the shifter let it bypass the theft-protection interlock.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer disables the overrides free.

issues.t: Turn signals flash like hazard lights (recall)
issues.sym: Using the turn signal makes lights on both sides flash.
issues.why: The turn signal flasher module relays could fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs a redesigned flasher module free.

issues.t: Power steering hose can burst (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden heavier steering, power steering fluid on the ground, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: Some pressure hoses were built out of spec and could split at full steering lock, which can cause a fire.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects and replaces the hose free.

issues.t: Driver door switch module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Window or lock switches on the driver door stop working or work on and off; in the worst case smoke or a burning smell from the door, even when parked.
issues.why: Fluid that gets into the driver door switch module corrodes its circuit board and can cause a short.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls. If the switches act up, park outside until a dealer replaces the module free.

issues.t: Headlights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: The low beams and daytime running lights stop working.
issues.why: The headlamp driver module can overheat and fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the module free.
